chapter_title: Chương 264: 0266【Hội thảo về Hệ thống Đăng ký Tên Thật trên Blog】

segments.title: Chương 264: 0266【Hội thảo về Hệ thống Đăng ký Tên Thật trên Blog】
segments.content:
Before the Internet Conference officially began, Chen Guiliang first attended a "Symposium on the Real-Name System for Chinese Blogs."

He had to go. Even if he didn't go himself, he would have had to send a company executive.

Because this was something like a collective meeting!

A Director-General from the Ministry of Information Industry was present, along with personnel from agencies like the Ministry of Truth and the Information Office.

Although Chen Guiliang ran an SNS website, he was on the invitation list for this symposium as long as it had a blog function.

Even the CEO of Cyworld, which was controlled by Koreans, was invited to attend.

The head of MSN China was also coming, because MSN's product, MySpace, also had a blog function. Qzone was designed to compete with MySpace.

When Chen Guiliang arrived at the venue, he found everyone with grim expressions, sitting in their seats waiting for the officials to appear.

The atmosphere was quite heavy, so much so that he didn't feel comfortable making a joke.

So, he took out his flashcards to memorize English words.

He had said he would pass the CET-4 this year, so he definitely would. It was just a matter of spending half an hour studying every day. In his last life, he passed it in his second year of university.

Fang Xingdong, hailed as the "Godfather of Chinese Blogs," came in smoking, puffing out clouds of smoke.

Fang Xingdong was having a very hard time these days. Last year, his Bokee.com had a market share of over 85%, but now it was about to drop below 30%. The new businesses he had added, like search engines and email, had all failed miserably.

This showed that he had truly fallen behind the times.

What era was this? And he was still adding new businesses like search engines and email.

The person Sina Blog sent today was Hou Xiaoqiang, the man who would later be in charge of Shanda Literature and Qidian for many years. His current title was Deputy Editor-in-Chief of Sina.com, responsible for overseeing the Sina Blog business.

Sina Blog was frantically inviting celebrities. The strategic decision was made by Editor-in-Chief Chen Tong, but the person actually running the operation was Hou Xiaoqiang.

Compared to Fang Xingdong's haggard appearance, Hou Xiaoqiang was beaming with success.

Even though he deliberately tried to look serious, he couldn't quite suppress his smile.

From Sohu Blog, the representative today was Sohu's Vice President and Editor-in-Chief, Li Shanyou, who was in charge of Sohu Blog's content.

Although NetEase Blog had not officially launched, NetEase's Vice President and Editor-in-Chief Li Yong also came.

Representing Qzone was Zheng Zhihao, who would later become the CEO of Maoyan.

In total, more than twenty heads of various blog and SNS websites, large and small, were present.

Even the CEO of Zhanzuo.com came. Although he had already decided to shut down the site, it was still undergoing financial liquidation and couldn't be closed right away.

The seating arrangement by the officials was very interesting.

Fang Xingdong, the former hegemon of the blogosphere, was arranged right at the front by the officials, despite his decline, by virtue of his seniority and connections.

After him were Sina Blog, Sohu Blog, MySpace, and Qzone.

Chen Guiliang was placed sixth, followed by NetEase Blog, and further back, the Korean guy from Cyworld…

Li Yong from NetEase Blog was the most relaxed, as their website hadn't even launched yet.

Seeing Chen Guiliang looking at something intently, Li Yong leaned his head over for a look and discovered they were English flashcards. His expression was one of amused disbelief, and he said in a low voice, "President Chen is truly a diligent learner."

Chen Guiliang said, "I haven't passed the CET-4 yet. I have to work harder this year."

"Pfft!"

Li Yong couldn't hold back a chuckle.

Zheng Zhihao from Qzone heard the sound and also leaned his head over to look, his expression quickly turning into one of mixed amusement and exasperation.

Just then, the officials began to file in.

The Director-General from the Ministry of Information Industry first introduced his colleagues from agencies like the Ministry of Truth and the Information Office, then introduced the enterprise representatives present, and thanked everyone for attending the symposium despite their busy schedules.

Then, the Director-General said, "With the rapid development of the internet, problems such as cybercrime, hacker and virus attacks, and the spread of inappropriate information have become increasingly prominent. As the industry's competent authority, the Ministry of Information Industry has always attached great importance to this. Since last year, the Ministry of Information Industry has done a great deal of work in strengthening internet governance, in accordance with the Scientific Outlook on Development and the requirements of building a harmonious society..."

"Blogs are one of the key areas of internet governance. Not including SNS websites, there are over 20 million blog authors in China, and over 100 million internet users have experience visiting blogs. If we include SNS websites, the number is countless..."

"While blogs have been developing, defamation, verbal abuse, pornography, leaking of secrets, and anti-social content have also become the dark side of blogging, greatly affecting the internet environment and hindering the development of a harmonious society..."

"Four months ago, the Internet Society of China released a draft for public comment of the 'Blog Service Self-Discipline Convention.' Netizens actively provided feedback, with supporters and opponents each holding their own ground, especially regarding the debate over a real-name system for blogs..."

"Today, we have invited many colleagues and enterprise representatives to talk face-to-face about the topic of a real-name system for blogs. We hope that you will all speak freely..."

The representatives of the major companies looked at each other, but no one spoke up first.

Chen Guiliang silently put away his flashcards.

"Let me start."

The official from the Ministry of Truth was a young man. He spoke up voluntarily, "Public opinion guidance is a matter of national importance. The current climate on blogs is particularly bad. There are people starting rumors, slandering others, and writing pornography on their blogs. They even spread anti-social FD rhetoric! And most websites do nothing about it. Coupled with internet anonymity, it's difficult to investigate the individuals responsible afterward. And it is because of internet anonymity that the audacity of these people is further fueled... A real-name system for blogs is now imperative!"

Fang Xingdong frowned deeply and couldn't help but state with fierce conviction, "A real-name system for blogs violates the fundamental spirit and laws of the internet. Once implemented, it will surely be the biggest mistake in the history of the Chinese internet!"

That was a very strong statement, and the officials' faces turned quite grim.

We put you in the first seat just so you could sing a contrary tune?

The Director-General said, "We also know that a direct real-name system is difficult to achieve. That's why the draft for public comment released four months ago only mentioned 'anonymous front-end, real-name back-end.' That is, when a blogger registers an account, they must provide their real name, ID number, contact information, and so on. This information would not be visible to other netizens; to the public, it would still appear anonymous."

Fang Xingdong still objected but said no more.

Kim Hee-young, the Korean, said, "We at Cyworld strongly support the real-name system. In our country, Korea, online information was once chaotic as well, especially baseless attacks against celebrities, which even led to singers and actors committing suicide. Earlier this year, our country passed relevant laws requiring individuals to use their real names when posting on websites."

"In fact, Cyworld in Korea implemented a full real-name system as early as two or three years ago. After Cyworld came to China, it has also been striving to implement a real-name system. Currently, 45% of Cyworld's Chinese users have real-name accounts."

"Now that the Chinese government wants to promote a real-name system, Cyworld will certainly do its best to cooperate!"

The officials were very pleased with such support from an international friend.

Several officials spoke in succession, all praising Cyworld as a model of China-Korea cooperation.

The representatives from major players like Sina, Sohu, NetEase, and Tencent remained silent, still waiting to see how things would unfold.

Shen Yang, the deputy editor-in-chief of Qianlong.com's blog channel, said, "This isn't a question of whether to implement it, but that it's fundamentally impossible to implement. Under the IPv4 architecture, China doesn't have enough IP addresses. Most are virtual dynamic IPs, so we can't bind IPs to ID numbers like they can in South Korea. Furthermore, there's no legislative basis, so it can't be enforced."

Li Shanyou from Sohu Blog said, "We can cooperate with the Ministry of Information Industry and guide bloggers to fill in their real information. But we can't force them, because even if they fill in random information, it would be difficult for Sohu to verify it."

The Director-General looked at Chen Guiliang, "Xiaonei.com now has a 100% real-name system. President Chen, perhaps you can share some of your experience."

Chen Guiliang said, "Xiaonei.com is a closed social network for campuses, which is different from the open social networking of other blogs and SNS. A Xiaonei account requires a student ID or degree number, but this is just a formality. The main enforcement relies on supervision from other users in the same class. If multiple users find that a certain person doesn't exist in their class, they can file a collective complaint... But even this has had its unexpected incidents."

"What kind of incidents?" an official from the Information Office asked curiously.

Chen Guiliang said, "Last year, a Peking University student stabbed his romantic rival dozens of times. I wonder if you've all heard about this news?"

Several people in the room nodded.

Chen Guiliang continued, "That student was a Beijing local. Although he got into Peking University, his academic ability was actually somewhat lacking. He couldn't keep up with his classmates' academic progress, and over time, he felt ostracized. So he started deliberately causing trouble. When the school held a dormitory cleanliness competition, his roommates were all busy cleaning, but he would intentionally dirty the floor..."

"He did many things like this and gradually became genuinely ostracized by the whole class. The students in his class got together, and with a two-thirds majority, they filed a collective complaint, saying he wasn't in their class and asking Xiaonei to ban his account. With two-thirds of his classmates filing a complaint, Xiaonei naturally determined it to be a fact and banned the person."

"One day, I was on my way to class, and this person stopped me, saying Xiaonei had unfairly banned his account, and even showed me his student ID. So I had Xiaonei restore his account. When the news of him killing someone came out, I was terrified in retrospect. If I hadn't restored his account, would that guy have come after me with a knife?"

"You should know, the rival he killed was his former roommate. And the victim had no idea he had ever offended him, nor did he know that his girlfriend was the object of the killer's secret crush and pursuit."

"Xiaonei can only claim to have a 99.99% real-name system; we wouldn't dare say it's 100% real. There are always special circumstances."

After hearing this, the Director-General nodded, "Achieving 99% is already very impressive. Is it possible for Hainei.com to implement a real-name system?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Hainei.com's model is a parallel system of real-name verification and anonymous social networking. If a celebrity wants to expand their influence, they can apply for real-name verification on Hainei, and we will carefully review their relevant documents. As for ordinary users, we have long been guiding them towards real-name registration and anonymous posting. But with so-called real-name registration, if they enter a fake name and ID number, it's also difficult for Hainei to verify."

Hou Xiaoqiang from Sina Blog said, "The most difficult thing right now is verification. Even if we were willing to commit the manpower and resources, we don't have the authority to verify it. If the government wants Sina Blog to have a real-name system, it must grant Sina the authority to verify customer information. What authority? The authority to check the household registration system! Can the government grant that?"

The officials were instantly speechless. Even they didn't have that authority, let alone an internet company.

Chen Guiliang suggested, "Instead of making internet companies implement a real-name system, it would be better to start with a real-name system for SIM cards. When anyone gets a card, they must bind their phone number to their ID card. That way, a real-name back-end for the internet becomes much easier to achieve. During registration, if they provide a phone number, we can just send a verification text message."

The officials nodded repeatedly, feeling that his point was reasonable.

"That won't work either," Zheng Zhihao said. "Many of our Qzone users are middle school and high school students. How would these students have cell phones? If they don't even have phones, how can they register with their real names via phone number?"

After discussing back and forth, they couldn't reach a conclusion in the end.

The major companies could only agree to cooperate with the government and try to guide users toward real-name registration, but they would not force users to post with their real names.

Chen Guiliang then elaborated on Hainei.com's graylist and blacklist system, which aimed to monitor users who repeatedly post malicious content while trying to protect freedom of speech online as much as possible.

The officials highly praised Hainei.com's approach.

Finally, the Director-General said, "Next month, the Ministry of Information Industry will formally adopt the real-name registration method for blogs. The back-end registration information for all of your blog or blog-like websites must be made more complete. To put it bluntly, even if the user fills it in randomly, they must fill in a name and ID number! Before the end of this year, all of your registration systems must be modified."

The representatives of the major companies spoke up one after another, expressing their support for the government.

This year, it wasn't just blogs; major forums were also invited to symposiums.

Even internet cafes were promoting a real-name system.

There was also something called a "Green Internet Project."

Even more ridiculous was Shi Yuzhu. This guy was too good at riding trends. He actually said that *ZT Online* would fully cooperate with the Green Internet Project and intended to make *ZT Online* a green online game, resolutely preventing minors from playing *ZT Online*.

Luo Taijun's NiuBo.com was about to go online. Given the outrageous opinions on NiuBo.com, launching at a time like this was practically flying in the face of the storm.
